manifest.query: SELECT type,name,tbl_name,COALESCE(sql,'') FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN ('table','index','trigger','view') AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY type,name
manifest.normalization: Replace every maximal SQL whitespace run with one ASCII space and trim leading and trailing whitespace.
manifest.serialization: UTF-8 JSON Lines; one compact object per line; fields ordered object_type,name,table_name,sql; LF after every line; SHA-256 covers the exact JSONL bytes.

internalManifest.query: SELECT type,name,tbl_name,COALESCE(sql,'') FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN ('table','index','trigger','view') AND name LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY type,name
internalManifest.allowlist: The six exact sqlite_autoindex_* objects generated by the frozen primary-key and UNIQUE constraints: privacy_egress_audit indexes 1 and 2, and index 1 for privacy_materials, privacy_receipts, privacy_redactions and privacy_schema_metadata. sqlite_stat*, sqlite_sequence and every other additional internal object fail closed.
internalManifest.serialization: The same normalized compact JSON Lines encoding as manifest; every allowed row has object_type=index and empty sql.

logicalManifest.tableOrdering: Table allowlist is sorted by unsigned lexicographic order of the table-name UTF-8 bytes.
logicalManifest.schemaEncoding: Each table section includes its manifest-normalized exact CREATE TABLE SQL and every PRAGMA table_xinfo field in ascending cid order: cid, name, exact declared type, not-null flag, default presence plus exact SQL text when present, primary-key ordinal, and hidden flag.
logicalManifest.rowOrdering: Rows are sorted by the unsigned lexicographic concatenation of full encoded PRIMARY KEY values in PK-ordinal order, then by the full encoded row; a table with no declared PK uses the full encoded row as its fallback sort key.
logicalManifest.valueEncoding: ADR-0002 exact tags: null 0x00; integer 0x01 plus i64 big-endian; real 0x02 plus IEEE-754 f64 bits big-endian; text/blob 0x03/0x04 plus u64 big-endian length and exact bytes.
logicalManifest.perTableHash: Diagnostic SHA-256 over the exact table section from its 0x10 marker through its final row, excluding the global domain and table count.
logicalManifest.businessPrimaryKeyEncoding: Domain and business-table count, followed for each table by its name, declared primary-key ordinal/name metadata, row count, and every canonical encoded primary-key sort key; all lengths and counts are u64 big-endian.
logicalManifest.businessRowEncoding: The complete canonical business table stream under the separate business-row domain, so row-value drift cannot be confused with either the logical/schema proof or the primary-key-only proof.
logicalManifest.output: Only domain-separated SHA-256 values, total row counts, and ordered table names/counts (plus diagnostic logical per-table hashes) are exposed; schema SQL, column metadata, row values, primary keys, raw identifiers, BLOBs and paths are never returned.

fixture.reason: Binary SQLite fixtures are deliberately excluded; tests construct the exact empty Privacy v1 database from the audited tag DDL.

validationRule: Production validation holds Windows handles for every root-to-parent ancestor directory with FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE and no FILE_SHARE_DELETE, plus FILE_SHARE_READ-only handles for the main database and every existing WAL/SHM/journal. Every handle uses FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT (directory handles also use FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS), remains live through both deferred validation transactions and final recapture, and is rebound to a fresh path identity. SQLite opens read-only/no-create with SQLITE_OPEN_NOFOLLOW, query_only and readonly_shm; its reported canonical main filename and read-only state must bind back to the guarded main-file identity. Validation compares every ordered normalized application schema object and every exact internal sqlite_autoindex allowlist object, validates the exact schema marker, quick_check, foreign_key_check, all v0.3.1 application data boundaries and the append-only egress hash chain, authenticates every protected review payload and protected receipt token with CurrentUser DPAPI, and proves data_version plus main/sidecar identity, length, mtime and SHA-256 stability. The logical, business, business-primary-key and business-row manifests are recomputed before and after the callback and again in the second transaction. Neither frozen schema-manifest SHA-256 substitutes for complete object comparison; the fixture SHA-256 identifies only the deterministic empty fixture. Non-Windows validation fails closed because this legacy source profile depends on Windows CurrentUser DPAPI and fixed-local Windows filesystem proofs.
